extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: SQuAD is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs posed by crowdworkers on 536 Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text (span) from the corresponding reading passage. The dataset is designed to challenge machines with a diverse range of question and answer types, requiring lexical, syntactic, and multi-sentence reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar; Jian Zhang; Konstantin Lopyrev; Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang. 2016. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv:1606.05250.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Passages were curated from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random and paragraphs extracted. Crowdworkers on the Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend) were then tasked with writing and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph. Additional answers were collected from separate crowdworkers for development and test set questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping; Manual Human Curator; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the additional answers collection phase, 2.6% of questions in the development and test sets were marked unanswerable by at least one crowdworker, meaning no answer span was provided for those questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks; 536 articles were sampled and 23,215 paragraphs extracted after stripping images, figures, tables, and short paragraphs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions per paragraph on Wikipedia passages; workers had to type questions in their own words (copy-paste from passage was disabled) and highlight the answer span in the paragraph. For additional answers, a separate set of crowdworkers selected the shortest span answering each question, or marked it unanswerable. Workers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, at least 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was assessed by treating the second answer as the human prediction and the remaining answers as ground truth; inter-annotator agreement yielded an F1 of 86.8% on the test set. Questions marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker were tracked (2.6% of dev/test questions).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 (1 original answer plus at least 2 additional answers for dev and test sets)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada; minimum 97% HIT acceptance rate; minimum 1000 HITs completed
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP (constituency parses, POS tags, NER tags used to automatically categorize answer types)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Articles were sampled from the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles by PageRank, which may overrepresent high-traffic topics; crowdworkers were required to be located in the United States or Canada, which may bias the language style of questions toward North American English speakers
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only 77.3% of correct answers in the development set are constituents in the constituency parse, placing an effective ceiling on the accuracy of methods that restrict candidates to constituents; 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker; questions with span-based answers are more constrained than more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of reading comprehension and question answering models; benchmarking machine comprehension of text; driving progress in natural language understanding
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. For the logistic regression model, when the correct answer of an example is not a constituent in the constituency parse, the shortest constituent containing the correct answer was used as the target during training. Additional answers (at least 2) were collected for each question in the development and test sets to make evaluation more robust and to assess human performance.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Wikipedia articles were filtered by selecting the top 10000 articles by PageRank, from which 536 were sampled uniformly at random. Individual paragraphs were extracted from each article, with images, figures, tables, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters discarded. Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. Copy-paste functionality was disabled during crowdsourcing to prevent direct copying of passage text into questions.
